name: Paneer Butter Masala
equipment: Small bowl for soaking cashews (hot water from a kettle or a small pan)
Measuring spoons (or use a regular teaspoon: 1 level tsp ≈ 5 ml)
Optional sieve, for a silky restaurant-smooth gravy

steps.title: Soak cashews
steps.text: Put 10 g (7–8) cashews in a small bowl and cover with 30 ml hot water.
steps.tip: hot water softens them faster than cold.
steps.visualCue: cashews look slightly swollen and softer
steps.cameraCheck: bowl of cashews submerged in water
steps.videoShot: hot water poured over cashews in a steel katori

steps.title: Chop onion
steps.text: Roughly chop 40 g (½ small) onion.
steps.visualCue: rough 2 cm pieces; size doesn't matter, it all gets blended

steps.title: Chop tomatoes
steps.text: Roughly chop 150 g (2 medium) tomatoes, removing the hard stem point.
steps.visualCue: juicy chunks

steps.title: Cube paneer
steps.text: Cut 100 g paneer into 2 cm cubes.
steps.visualCue: even cubes that hold their shape
steps.videoShot: paneer block sliced into strips, then cubes

steps.title: Soften paneer
steps.text: Cover the cubes with warm (not boiling) water and leave them.
steps.tip: this keeps store-bought paneer soft and stops it going rubbery in the curry.
steps.visualCue: cubes submerged

steps.title: Measure spices
steps.text: On a small plate, put ¾ tsp Kashmiri chilli powder, ½ tsp coriander powder, a pinch of turmeric, ¼ tsp garam masala, ½ tsp sugar, ⅓ tsp salt and ½ tsp kasuri methi, each in its own little heap.
steps.visualCue: separate heaps of spice
steps.videoShot: spoon dropping each spice onto the plate

steps.title: Heat oil
steps.text: Put the kadai on medium heat and add 1 tsp (5 ml) oil.
steps.visualCue: oil shimmers and flows freely when you tilt the pan

steps.title: Sauté onion
steps.text: Add the chopped onion and stir.
steps.visualCue: onion turns soft and translucent at the edges, not brown

steps.title: Add ginger-garlic paste
steps.text: Add 1 tsp ginger-garlic paste and stir.
steps.visualCue: raw garlic smell fades

steps.title: Add tomatoes and drained cashews
steps.text: Add the chopped tomatoes and the cashews (drain off the soaking water, but save it).
steps.visualCue: pan full of tomato chunks with cashews mixed through
steps.videoShot: tomatoes and cashews tipped into the pan

steps.title: Cook tomatoes down
steps.text: Cover and cook on medium-low, stirring every minute or two.
steps.visualCue: tomatoes are completely mushy and break when pressed with the spatula
steps.cameraCheck: the pan, pressing a tomato with the spatula

steps.title: Cool the mixture
steps.text: Switch off the heat and tip the mixture onto a plate to cool.
steps.tip: never blend piping-hot food in a closed jar. Steam can blow the lid off.
steps.visualCue: warm, no longer steaming hard
steps.cameraCheck: the plate of cooked tomato mixture
steps.videoShot: mixture spread on a steel plate

steps.title: Blend
steps.text: Put the mixture in the small mixer jar with the saved cashew water and blend until completely smooth.
steps.tip: for a restaurant-silky gravy, push it through a sieve (optional).
steps.visualCue: smooth, bright orange-red purée with no flecks of cashew
steps.videoShot: purée pouring off a spoon in a smooth ribbon

steps.title: Melt butter
steps.text: Wipe out the kadai, put it on low heat and add 2 tsp (10 g) butter.
steps.visualCue: butter melted and foaming gently, not brown

steps.title: Temper bay leaf
steps.text: Add 1 bay leaf to the butter.
steps.visualCue: leaf sizzles and smells fragrant

steps.title: Add spice powders
steps.text: Add the chilli powder, coriander powder and turmeric and stir.
steps.tip: keep the heat low. Spices burn in seconds.
steps.visualCue: butter turns deep red; smells toasty, not burnt
steps.videoShot: red butter swirled with the spatula

steps.title: Add purée
steps.text: Pour in the blended purée straight away and stir.
steps.visualCue: sauce bubbles gently and spits a little
steps.videoShot: purée poured into the red butter

steps.title: Cook the gravy
steps.text: Cook on medium-low, stirring often, partly covered (it splutters).
steps.visualCue: gravy darkens a shade, thickens, and tiny drops of butter appear at the edges
steps.cameraCheck: the pan edge showing the butter separating
steps.videoShot: thick gravy bubbling with shiny edges

steps.title: Season
steps.text: Add the salt and sugar and stir.
steps.visualCue: dissolved; taste: tangy, mildly sweet, mildly spicy

steps.title: Loosen with water
steps.text: Add 60–80 ml (about ⅓ cup) water and stir. Bring to a gentle simmer.
steps.visualCue: gravy coats the back of a spoon and drips slowly
steps.cameraCheck: the back of the spoon coated in gravy
steps.videoShot: finger line drawn through gravy on a spoon

steps.title: Add paneer
steps.text: Drain the paneer and add the cubes. Stir gently.
steps.visualCue: every cube coated in orange gravy

steps.title: Simmer paneer
steps.text: Simmer on low.
steps.tip: don't simmer longer than about 5 minutes, or the paneer toughens.
steps.visualCue: paneer is warmed through and soft; gravy bubbles lazily

steps.title: Add kasuri methi
steps.text: Crush ½ tsp kasuri methi between your palms over the pan and stir.
steps.visualCue: aroma becomes noticeably "restaurant-like"

steps.title: Add garam masala
steps.text: Sprinkle in ¼ tsp garam masala and stir.
steps.visualCue: evenly mixed

steps.title: Finish with cream
steps.text: Turn the heat off. Swirl in 1 tbsp (15 ml) fresh cream.
steps.tip: adding cream with the heat off stops it splitting.
steps.visualCue: gravy turns a paler, glossy orange
steps.videoShot: white cream swirled through orange gravy

steps.title: Remove bay leaf and plate
steps.text: Take out the bay leaf, spoon the curry into a bowl and top with chopped coriander (optional).
steps.visualCue: glossy orange curry with visible paneer cubes
steps.videoShot: slow pan across the finished bowl

reasons: Paneer gives good protein (~23 g) and the tomato base brings lycopene and some fibre. But fat is high (~43 g, much of it saturated from paneer, butter and cream), and the dish has almost no vegetables beyond tomato and onion. This version uses 10 g butter + 5 ml oil + 1 tbsp cream. Restaurant versions commonly use 2–4 times that butter and cream, plus more sugar and salt, often with a heavy butter naan on the side.

researchRating.basis: one of India's most-ordered and most-cooked paneer dishes. Recipes are rated very highly by home cooks, though a recurring complaint is that versions can taste too sweet or heavy.

storage: Fridge-safe in an airtight container for up to 2 days. Freezer: up to 1 month (est.), though the paneer turns slightly spongy and the cream may separate a little. Reheating: gently on the stove on low with 2–3 tbsp water, stirring, until just hot. In the microwave, use 1-minute bursts and stir in between. Don't boil hard.
leftoverRemix: Paneer makhani kathi roll. Simmer the leftover curry until thick, mash a few paneer cubes, then spread on a warm roti with sliced onion, a squeeze of lemon and green chutney, and roll it up for a quick lunch.
burnOff: about 7.7 km of running (at ~70 kcal/km), or about 11 km of brisk walking (at ~50 kcal/km, est.).
